The perceptron is from 1958; backpropagation, as it is used today, became popular in 1986; convolutional networks applied to recognising digits, in 1989. That is: this block's central ideas are between thirty and seventy years old. What changed from 2012 on was not the mathematics but three things at once: enormous data sets appeared, graphics cards made matrix multiplications cheap, and a few practical details —ReLU, better initialisations, Adam— made trainable what used to get stuck.
